items.text:
Pull request #482 from Priya Raman touches the fare comparison service in the booking flow, and I've flagged two concerns before we merge.

First, the currency rounding in `convert_fare()` now truncates instead of rounding to the nearest cent, which will drift on multi-leg itineraries. Second, the new supplier timeout is hardcoded at 8 seconds; that should come from config so ops can tune it per market without a deploy.

Everything else looks good — tests cover the boundary cases, and the staging run against the Sandpiper Air sandbox came back clean. Priya, can you address the rounding issue and pull the timeout into `config/suppliers.yaml`? Happy to re-review once that's pushed.

intent.requested_action: fix rounding and move timeout to config before merge

items.text:
Finance team, here's the Q3 forecast for the travel booking platform, focused on the hotel and flight bundles.

We're projecting net revenue of €4.2M for the quarter, up 11% on Q2, driven mostly by the new multi-city itinerary builder. Costs rise in step because supplier commissions on long-haul fares went up in June. Marketing spend stays flat at €380k, assuming the Q3 campaign slips to Q4.

The main risk is FX: about a third of bookings settle in GBP, and if sterling weakens another 4% against the euro our gross margin drops roughly 120 basis points. I'd suggest we hold a €150k contingency buffer rather than re-price bundles mid-quarter.

Open question for Dana: do we model the Sandpiper Air renegotiation as a 3% or 5% reduction? Everything in the sheet uses 3% for now.

intent.requested_action: confirm the Sandpiper assumption and finance team to weigh a contingency buffer

items.text: Posting this to the supplier forum because we can't be the only ones hitting it. Sandpiper Air changed their fare-feed schema on 12 June and our booking assistant has been quietly dropping the baggage allowances ever since. The docs still show `bag_allow` as a string, but the feed now sends an object, so anything reading it as a string gets null. We patched it in about an hour once we found it. If your integration caches fares, flush the cache after the patch or you'll keep serving stale allowances for the rest of the day.

intent.requested_action: patch the schema change and flush cached fares
